title: SLO-led regional surge containment proxy and streaming continuity strategy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: Our hosted API is active-active across three regions. During regional capacity spikes or noisy-neighbor events we observe cascading backpressure: bursty request arrivals overwhelm local pool, SLOs degrade, aggressive global rebalancing causes large-scale stream disconnects and token cache mismatch. Long-lived streaming sessions (HTTP chunked streaming / gRPC / WebSocket proxies) are vulnerable to abrupt drains, causing customer-visible errors and session restarts. We need a strategy that (1) protects global SLOs, (2) contains regional surges without mass session loss, (3) provides deterministic circuit-breaker behavior and controlled load-shedding, and (4) maintains resumability for streaming sessions.
background: Previous work improved per-request graceful failover and KV-sync, but customers still report degraded UX for streaming features during region drains. Existing circuit breakers are binary and applied at service boundary; they lack SLO-sensitivity and session-awareness. Readouts from console/telemetry show correlated 5xx spikes and connection churn during uncontrolled traffic shifts. We want a minimal proactive proxy layer at the edge gateways that enforces SLO-driven containment and provides lightweight session anchoring for continuity.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled containment proxy deployed as canary in us-west-2 and eu-central-1
During a synthetic region surge (2x traffic), global 5xx rate is reduced by >=80% compared to baseline without proxy
Median tail latency for non-streaming requests remains within SLO (p95 < configured SLO) during shift windows
Streaming session resume success >=95% after graceful handover (client reconnect within 30s) with no token loss
Circuit-breaker opens and performs priority-aware shedding (low-priority requests shed first) under overload
Operational toggles exist for immediate global drain, weighted drain, and dry-run telemetry mode
Runbook and playbook documented and validated with on-call run-through
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Build lightweight proxy component that sits in front of regional gateway and evaluates per-region SLO telemetry (error rate, queue depth, CPU/mem headroom)
Phase 1a: Implement SLO evaluator that computes a single region health score every 10s (inputs: 5xx rate, p95 latency, connection churn rate, GPU utilization). Health score is a 0-100 integer.
Phase 1b: Implement circuit policy: open when 5xx_rate > 3% AND health_score < 40 for 120s; half-open probe every 30s with controlled probe QPS (10% of normal).
Phase 2: Add priority buckets: control-plane (admin), paid customers, free-tier; shedding order = free -> paid -> control-plane (last). Shedding thresholds configurable per-customer tier.

Phase 3: Streaming continuity: implement session-anchor hints written to regional session map (dual-write to local in-memory map + durable checkpoint in S3-like store every 10s) to allow quick resume in another region. Checkpoint includes minimal stream offsets and model KV cache fingerprint, not full KV values.

Phase 4: Traffic shift modes: weighted-drain (gradual 5-20% stepdowns per minute), emergency-evacuate (fast, aggressive routing), and soft-proxy-redirect (proxy responds with 307 to clients that support sticky hinting).

Phase 5: Telemetry and dashboards: per-region health score, circuit state, shed rates per priority, streaming-resume success metric, token-fingerprint mismatch rate. Add alerting for open circuit > 5 min or resume_rate <90%
Canary plan: deploy to 2% of ingress in us-west-2 for 48 hours, run synthetic surge test, then expand to eu-central-1 if metrics pass
Rollback: revert to legacy routing by disabling proxy and removing route prefixes from gateway config; feature toggle in console + infra runbook
Integration: must be compatible with existing KV-cache prefixing and model variant fallback. Work with runtime team to expose KV fingerprint API for checkpointing.
Backward compatibility: clients that do not support redirect/hints should still be served; proxy must not cause additional latency > 10ms median on non-peak traffic.
design_considerations: Trade-off: full KV sync vs fingerprint checkpointing. Full sync is expensive and increases failover time; fingerprinting reduces data transfer at cost of potentially requiring model cold-start in target region. We choose fingerprint + optional prefetch on resume for hot sessions.

Trade-off: active session anchoring vs stateless routing. Anchoring improves resume rate but increases cross-region metadata writes; we'll keep metadata minimal and TTL-based (30 minutes) to limit storage overhead.
Circuit granularity: service-level vs customer-level. We'll support both, defaulting to per-service circuits and enabling per-customer circuits for enterprise tenants behind dedicated config.
Safety: avoid controller oscillation by adding hysteresis to health_score evaluation and using weighted moving averages for metrics.
Security: session anchors and tokens must be encrypted in transit and at rest. Use existing KMS/HSM key for checkpoint encryption.
risks_mitigations: Risk: Anchor metadata divergence can lead to incorrect resume and token mismatch. Mitigation: include KV fingerprint and token version; on resume if mismatch, fallback to safe disconnect with descriptive error and automated rollback of session attempt.
Risk: Proxy adds latency on cold paths. Mitigation: introduce fast-path bypass when region health is good and no session hints are present.

Risk: Priority shedding could impact free-tier features customers rely on. Mitigation: expose customer-impact flag and schedule coordinated communications for rollout; provide emergency suspend toggle for critical customers.
